subproblems.title: Currents annihilate test forms supported off their support (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every set U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n and every test form ω ∈ TestFormOn U n: if tsupport ω is disjoint from spt T = U ∖ zeroRegion(T), then T(ω) = 0. (Reuse, with identical frozen Lean type, of the comparator-accepted declaration isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n)) T.support → T ω = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the accepted proof of the reused declaration isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support (node root.isoperimetric-a1.vanish_off_support-a1), reproduced verbatim; the frozen Lean type is identical, so the comparator-accepted declaration is reused.

Notation. For T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, `T.VanishesOn W` means T(η) = 0 for every η ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport η ⊆ W. Let 𝒲 be the family of all W ⊆ ℝ^P with W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W. By definition T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲 and T.support = U ∖ T.zeroRegion.

1. Let K := tsupport ω. Since ω ∈ TestFormOn U n, ω is C^∞, has compact support (so K is compact, in particular closed) and K ⊆ U.
2. K ⊆ ⋃𝒲. Let x ∈ K. Then x ∈ U, and x ∉ T.support by the disjointness hypothesis, i.e. x ∉ U ∖ T.zeroRegion; hence x ∈ T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲.
3. Every member of 𝒲 is open, so by compactness of K there are finitely many W_1, …, W_r ∈ 𝒲 (r ≥ 0; r = 0 when K = ∅) with K ⊆ W_1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ W_r (e.g. `IsCompact.elim_finite_subcover_image`; it is convenient to index the cover by the resulting finite subfamily rather than by Fin r).
4. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P), with the model with corners 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P), is a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, σ-compact smooth manifold, and K is closed and covered by the open sets W_i (i ranging over the finite index set of step 3). Hence there is a smooth partition of unity on K subordinate to (W_i): C^∞ functions ψ_1, …, ψ_r : ℝ^P → [0, 1] with tsupport ψ_i ⊆ W_i for every i and Σ_i ψ_i(x) = 1 for every x ∈ K (Mathlib `SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`; a real-valued `ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ^P) 𝓘(ℝ)` function of class C^∞ is `ContDiff ℝ ∞` by `contMDiff_iff_contDiff`).
5. For each i put η_i(x) := ψ_i(x) • ω(x). Then η_i is C^∞ (a C^∞ scalar function times a C^∞ form). If ω(x) = 0 or ψ_i(x) = 0 then η_i(x) = 0, so support η_i ⊆ support ω ∩ support ψ_i; taking closures, tsupport η_i ⊆ K ∩ tsupport ψ_i ⊆ U ∩ W_i. In particular η_i has compact support (closed subset of the compact K). Thus η_i ∈ TestFormOn U n and tsupport η_i ⊆ W_i.
6. Since W_i ∈ 𝒲, T vanishes on W_i, so T(η_i) = 0 for every i.
7. ω = Σ_i η_i in TestFormOn U n (checked pointwise). If x ∈ K, then Σ_i ψ_i(x) • ω(x) = (Σ_i ψ_i(x)) • ω(x) = ω(x). If x ∉ K, then x ∉ support ω, so ω(x) = 0 and every η_i(x) = 0. (If r = 0 then K = ∅, ω = 0 and both sides are 0.)
8. T acts ℝ-linearly on TestFormOn U n (T.toCurrent is a linear map), so by steps 6 and 7, T(ω) = Σ_i T(η_i) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport ω is a compact subset of U disjoint from spt T, hence contained in the zero region, i.e. covered by the open sets W on which T vanishes.
Extract a finite subcover W_1, …, W_r of tsupport ω.
Take a smooth partition of unity ψ_1, …, ψ_r on tsupport ω subordinate to the W_i (Mathlib SmoothPartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate).
Each ψ_i • ω is a test form in U with tsupport in W_i, so T(ψ_i • ω) = 0.
ω = Σ_i ψ_i • ω pointwise, so T(ω) = 0 by linearity.

subproblems.title: Mass estimate |T(ω)| ≤ M_W(T)·sup|ω| (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, W ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ GeometricCurrentOn U n, ω ∈ TestFormOn U n and B, C ∈ ℝ with B ≥ 0, T.massOn W ≤ ofReal B, tsupport ω ⊆ W and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ C for every x. Then |T(ω)| ≤ B·C. (Reuse, with identical frozen Lean type, of the comparator-accepted declaration cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (B C : ℝ), 0 ≤ B → T.massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) x) ≤ C) → |T ω| ≤ B * C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the accepted proof of the reused declaration cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le (node root.compactness_mass_bounds-a1.mass_bound-a1), reproduced verbatim; the frozen Lean type is identical, so the comparator-accepted declaration is reused. It is stated with an explicit real bound B for M_W(T) and an explicit pointwise bound C for |ω|, which avoids dividing by sup|ω| and any case distinction on ω = 0.

Notation: for an n-covector α, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P, I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)},…,e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i. M_W(T) = T.massOn W is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ψ)) over ψ ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W = {ψ ∈ TestFormOn U n : tsupport ψ ⊆ W and |ψ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x}.

1. (Homogeneity.) For t ∈ ℝ and a covector α, |tα| = |t|·|α|. Each coefficient satisfies (tα)(e_I) = t·α(e_I), so the sum of squares is multiplied by t², and √(t²S) = |t|·√S.
2. (C ≥ 0.) 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ C.
3. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix a real c > C, so c > 0. Let s ∈ {c⁻¹, −c⁻¹}. TestFormOn U n is a real submodule, so s•ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Also tsupport(s•ω) ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, and by Step 1, |(s•ω)(x)| = c⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ C/c ≤ 1 for every x. Hence s•ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, and GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn gives ENNReal.ofReal(T(s•ω)) ≤ M_W(T) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B.
4. (Unpacking.) Because B ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ ENNReal.ofReal B implies a ≤ B (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff). By linearity T(s•ω) = s·T(ω). Therefore c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B and −c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B. Multiplying by c > 0 gives T(ω) ≤ Bc and −T(ω) ≤ Bc, i.e. |T(ω)| ≤ B·c. This holds for every c > C.
5. (Letting c ↓ C.) Let ε > 0 and c := C + ε/(B+1) > C. Step 4 gives |T(ω)| ≤ BC + Bε/(B+1) ≤ BC + ε. Since ε > 0 is arbitrary, |T(ω)| ≤ B·C (le_of_forall_pos_le_add). ∎
proof_key_steps: |tα| = |t|·|α| and C ≥ 0.
For c > C, ±c⁻¹ω is mass-admissible for W, so ±c⁻¹T(ω) ≤ B by le_massOn and B ≥ 0.
Hence |T(ω)| ≤ B·c for every c > C; let c decrease to C.

subproblems.title: Covector evaluation bound |α(τ)| ≤ P^n |α| (reused accepted lemma)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, every n-covector α on ℝ^P and every τ_1, …, τ_n ∈ ℝ^P with ‖τ_j‖ ≤ 1: |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ P^n · covectorEuclideanNorm(α). (Reuse, with identical frozen Lean type, of the comparator-accepted declaration isoperimetric_abs_covector_apply_le.)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Eucl P) n) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P), (∀ j, ‖τ j‖ ≤ 1) → |α τ| ≤ (P : ℝ) ^ n * covectorEuclideanNorm α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the accepted proof of the reused declaration isoperimetric_abs_covector_apply_le (node root.isoperimetric-a1.covector_eval_bound-a1), reproduced verbatim; the frozen Lean type is identical, so the comparator-accepted declaration is reused.

Notation. e_a := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ a = EuclideanSpace.single a 1 for a ∈ Fin P; for f : Fin n → Fin P write e_f := (e_{f(1)}, …, e_{f(n)}) and α(e_f) for α applied to this tuple. N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α = sqrt(Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} (if I is strictly increasing then α(e_I)² else 0)) ≥ 0.

1. Claim: |α(e_f)| ≤ N(α) for every f : Fin n → Fin P.
 (a) If f is not injective, choose i ≠ i' with f(i) = f(i'). The tuple e_f has equal entries in the distinct positions i and i', and α is alternating, so α(e_f) = 0 ≤ N(α) (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_eq`).
 (b) If f is injective, let σ := Tuple.sort f, a permutation of Fin n such that f ∘ σ is monotone (`Tuple.monotone_sort`). The map I := f ∘ σ is monotone and injective, hence strictly increasing. Since e_I = e_f ∘ σ and α is alternating, α(e_f ∘ σ) = sign(σ) · α(e_f) (`AlternatingMap.map_perm` applied to α.toAlternatingMap), so |α(e_f)| = |α(e_I)|. As I is strictly increasing, α(e_I)² is one of the nonnegative summands whose sum is N(α)², so α(e_I)² ≤ N(α)² and |α(e_I)| = sqrt(α(e_I)²) ≤ N(α).
2. Expansion. For each j, τ_j = Σ_{a ∈ Fin P} τ_j(a) • e_a (expansion in the standard orthonormal basis). By multilinearity of α (expansion of a multilinear map applied to sums and extraction of scalars: `ContinuousMultilinearMap.map_sum` and `map_smul_univ` applied to α.toContinuousMultilinearMap):
 α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = Σ_{f : Fin n → Fin P} (Π_{j ∈ Fin n} τ_j(f(j))) · α(e_f).
3. For every j and a, |τ_j(a)| ≤ ‖τ_j‖ ≤ 1 (a coordinate of a Euclidean vector is bounded by its norm, `PiLp.norm_apply_le`). Hence |Π_j τ_j(f(j))| = Π_j |τ_j(f(j))| ≤ 1 for every f (a product of numbers in [0, 1], `Finset.prod_le_one₀`).
4. By the triangle inequality and steps 1 and 3, |α(τ_1, …, τ_n)| ≤ Σ_f |Π_j τ_j(f(j))| · |α(e_f)| ≤ Σ_f N(α) = card(Fin n → Fin P) · N(α) = P^n · N(α). (For n = 0 the sum has the single empty f, the product is 1 and the bound reads |α()| ≤ N(α).) ∎
proof_key_steps: |α(e_f)| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α for every f : Fin n → Fin P: zero if f is not injective; otherwise sort f by a permutation σ and use α(e_f ∘ σ) = sign σ · α(e_f).
Expand α(τ) multilinearly in the standard basis: a sum over the P^n maps f of (Π_j τ_j(f j)) α(e_f).
Each coefficient satisfies |Π_j τ_j(f j)| ≤ 1 because |τ_j(a)| ≤ ‖τ_j‖ ≤ 1.
Summing gives |α(τ)| ≤ P^n · covectorEuclideanNorm α.

1. (Interior product as a bounded bilinear map.) For α ∈ Λ_{k+1}, Mathlib's α.curryLeft ∈ E →L[ℝ] Λ_k satisfies (α.curryLeft w)(v) = α(w, v) (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply`; Matrix.vecCons = Fin.cons) and ‖α.curryLeft‖ = ‖α‖ (`norm_curryLeft`). Let 𝔅 : Λ_{k+1} →L[ℝ] (E →L[ℝ] Λ_k), 𝔅(α) := α.curryLeft (the linear isometry `ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeftLI` as a continuous linear map). Then ‖𝔅‖ ≤ 1 and ‖𝔅(α)(w)‖ ≤ ‖α‖‖w‖.
2. (The integrand.) Define F : ℝ × E → Λ_k by F(t,x) := t^a • 𝔅(ω(t•x))(x). F is C^∞ on ℝ × E: (t,x) ↦ t•x is C^∞ (bounded bilinear), ω is C^∞, (α,x) ↦ 𝔅(α)(x) is a bounded bilinear map, t ↦ t^a is a polynomial, and compositions/products of C^∞ maps are C^∞ (ContDiff.comp, ContDiff.clm_apply, ContDiff.smul). For every v ∈ E^k, F(t,x)(v) = t^a ω(t•x)(x, v).
3. (Differentiation under the integral sign.) Claim: let V be a finite-dimensional real normed space and G : ℝ × E → V a C^∞ map, and g(x) := ∫_0^1 G(t,x) dt. Then g is C^∞ and D^jg(x) = ∫_0^1 ∂^jG(t,x) dt for every j ∈ ℕ and x ∈ E.
 (a) For each j, (t,x) ↦ ∂^jG(t,x) is continuous: ∂^jG(t,x) is the full iterated derivative D^jG(t,x) composed, in each of its j arguments, with the fixed continuous linear embedding E → ℝ × E, h ↦ (0, h) (chain rule `ContinuousLinearMap.iteratedFDeriv_comp_right` applied to z ↦ G((t,0) + (0,z)), exactly as in SimonGMT's `iteratedFDeriv_fixedSupportParameterSlice`), and (t,x) ↦ D^jG(t,x) is continuous because G is C^∞ (`ContDiff.continuous_iteratedFDeriv`).
 (b) Let g_j(x) := ∫_0^1 ∂^jG(t,x) dt. Fix j and x₀. By (a), K := sup{‖∂^{j+1}G(t,x)‖ : t ∈ [0,1], ‖x − x₀‖ ≤ 1} < ∞ (a continuous function on a compact set). The Fréchet derivative of x ↦ ∂^jG(t,x) corresponds to ∂^{j+1}G(t,x) under the canonical currying isometry (`continuousMultilinearCurryLeftEquiv`, `iteratedFDeriv_succ_eq_comp_left`), so its norm is ≤ K for t ∈ [0,1], ‖x − x₀‖ < 1. By `intervalIntegral.hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le` (neighbourhood B(x₀,1), constant bound K; measurability and integrability in t from continuity), g_j is Fréchet differentiable at x₀ and its derivative is ∫_0^1 D_x(∂^jG)(t,x₀) dt, which is the image of g_{j+1}(x₀) under the currying isometry (a continuous linear equivalence commutes with the integral). By (a) and `intervalIntegral.continuous_parametric_intervalIntegral_of_continuous`, every g_j is continuous.
 (c) Hence g = g_0 is differentiable with derivative corresponding to g_1, and by induction on j, D^jg = g_j for all j (`iteratedFDeriv_succ_eq_comp_left`); since every g_j is continuous and differentiable, g is C^∞ (`contDiff_of_differentiable_iteratedFDeriv`).
4. Define ψ(x) := ∫_0^1 F(t,x) dt ∈ Λ_k (Bochner interval integral of a continuous function). By Step 3 with V := Λ_k and G := F, ψ is C^∞ and D^jψ(x) = ∫_0^1 ∂^jF(t,x) dt for all j and x.
5. (Formula (i).) For fixed v ∈ E^k, evaluation at v is a continuous linear map Λ_k → ℝ (`ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply`), so it commutes with the interval integral (`ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm`). Hence ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 F(t,x)(v) dt = ∫_0^1 t^a ω(t•x)(x, v) dt.
6. (Formula (ii).) By the chain rule for x ↦ ω(t•x) (derivative w ↦ Dω(tx)[t•w] = t·Dω(tx)[w]) and the product rule for the bounded bilinear map 𝔅, ∂^1F(t,x)[w] = t^a • ( t • 𝔅(Dω(tx)[w])(x) + 𝔅(ω(tx))(w) ). By Step 4 with j = 1, Dψ(x) = ∫_0^1 ∂^1F(t,x) dt; applying the continuous linear maps “evaluate at w” and then “evaluate at v”, which commute with the integral, gives Dψ(x)[w](v) = ∫_0^1 t^a ( t·(Dω(tx)[w])(x, v) + ω(tx)(w, v) ) dt.
7. (Bound (iii).) Let j, R, D be as in (iii), ‖x‖ ≤ R (so R ≥ 0) and t ∈ [0,1]. Put g_t(z) := ω(t•z) = ω ∘ (t•id). By `ContinuousLinearMap.iteratedFDeriv_comp_right`, D^lg_t(x) = D^lω(t•x) ∘ (t•id, …, t•id), hence ‖D^lg_t(x)‖ ≤ |t|^l‖D^lω(t•x)‖ ≤ D for l ≤ j (`ContinuousMultilinearMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le`; ‖t•x‖ ≤ ‖x‖ ≤ R). Since F(t,·) = t^a • 𝔅(g_t(·))(id(·)), the Leibniz bound for bounded bilinear maps (`ContinuousLinearMap.norm_iteratedFDeriv_le_of_bilinear`) gives ‖∂^jF(t,x)‖ ≤ t^a‖𝔅‖ Σ_{i=0}^{j} C(j,i)‖D^ig_t(x)‖‖D^{j−i}id(x)‖. Now ‖D^0id(x)‖ = ‖x‖ ≤ R, ‖D^1id(x)‖ = ‖id‖ ≤ 1 and D^lid = 0 for l ≥ 2 (id is continuous linear), so only i = j and i = j − 1 contribute: ‖∂^jF(t,x)‖ ≤ D·R + j·D = (R + j)·D (using t^a ≤ 1 and ‖𝔅‖ ≤ 1; for j = 0 only the first term occurs). By Step 4, ‖D^jψ(x)‖ = ‖∫_0^1 ∂^jF(t,x) dt‖ ≤ (R + j)·D (`intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const`). This is (iii), and ψ satisfies (i)–(iii). ∎
proof_key_steps: Write the integrand as F(t,x) = t^a • (ω(t•x)).curryLeft x, a jointly C^∞ map ℝ × ℝ^P → Λ_k built from the norm-1 bilinear interior product.

Differentiation under the integral sign over [0,1] (intervalIntegral.hasFDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_of_fderiv_le with compact-set bounds, induction on j): ψ := ∫_0^1 F(t,·) dt is C^∞ and D^jψ = ∫_0^1 ∂_x^j F dt.
Evaluating at v (a continuous linear map commuting with the integral) gives formula (i); the product and chain rules give the first-derivative formula (ii).
Leibniz bound for the bilinear interior product with D^l(ω(t·)) = t^l D^lω(t·)∘(t•) and ‖D^l id‖ ∈ {‖x‖, ≤1, 0} gives ‖∂_x^jF(t,x)‖ ≤ (R + j)D on B̄_R(0), hence (iii).

subproblems.title: Radial homotopy formula for forms
subproblems.statement: (a) Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let φ be a C^∞ (k+1)-form on ℝ^P, ψ any k-form and χ any (k+1)-form on ℝ^P such that Dψ(x)[w](v) = ∫_0^1 t^k ( t·(Dφ(tx)[w])(x, v) + φ(tx)(w, v) ) dt for all x, w ∈ ℝ^P, v ∈ (ℝ^P)^k, and χ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^{k+1} dφ(tx)(x, v) dt for all x ∈ ℝ^P, v ∈ (ℝ^P)^{k+1}. Then χ(x) + dψ(x) = φ(x) for every x (radial homotopy formula H(dφ) + d(H′φ) = φ). (b) Let φ be a C^∞ 0-form and χ a 0-form on ℝ^P with χ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^0 dφ(tx)(x, v) dt (v the empty tuple). Then χ(x) = φ(x) − φ(0) for every x. Here d = Mathlib's extDeriv (dψ(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin (Dψ(x)), defined for every function), D = fderiv, and (x, v) = Fin.cons x v.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P k : ℕ) (φ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (k + 1)) (ψ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) k) (χ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (k + 1)), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) φ → (∀ (x w : Eucl P) (v : Fin k → Eucl P), fderiv ℝ ψ x w v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ k * (t * fderiv ℝ φ (t • x) w (Fin.cons x v) + φ (t • x) (Fin.cons w v))) → (∀ (x : Eucl P) (v : Fin (k + 1) → Eucl P), χ x v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ (k + 1) * extDeriv φ (t • x) (Fin.cons x v)) → ∀ x, χ x + extDeriv ψ x = φ x) ∧ (∀ (P : ℕ) (φ χ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) 0), ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) φ → (∀ (x : Eucl P) (v : Fin 0 → Eucl P), χ x v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ 0 * extDeriv φ (t • x) (Fin.cons x v)) → ∀ x, χ x = φ x - φ 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Part I, item 2 of the parent proof (“the radial homotopy formula H(dφ) + d(H′φ) = φ … (Cartan's formula for the homotopy (t,x) ↦ tx …)” for m ≥ 1, and “H(dφ)(x) = ∫_0^1 (d/dt)φ(tx) dt = φ(x) − φ(0)” for m = 0), written out as a direct computation.

Conventions. E := ℝ^P; for any function ψ : E → Λ_k, Mathlib defines extDeriv ψ x := alternatizeUncurryFin (fderiv ℝ ψ x), so by `ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_apply`, dψ(x)(u) = Σ_{i=0}^{k} (−1)^i (Dψ(x)[u_i])(removeNth i u) for u ∈ E^{k+1}; no differentiability of ψ is needed for this identity. (x, v) := Fin.cons x v.

Part (a). Fix x ∈ E and u ∈ E^{k+1}; it suffices to prove χ(x)(u) + dψ(x)(u) = φ(x)(u). Put û_j := removeNth j u ∈ E^k for j = 0, …, k and, for t ∈ ℝ, A(t) := Dφ(tx)[x](u), B_j(t) := Dφ(tx)[u_j](x, û_j), C_j(t) := φ(tx)(u_j, û_j), D(t) := φ(tx)(u). These are continuous in t (φ and Dφ are continuous since φ is C^∞, t ↦ tx is continuous, and evaluations are continuous linear), hence interval integrable on [0,1].
1. (Expansion of dφ.) For every t, dφ(tx)(x, u) = A(t) + Σ_{j=0}^{k} (−1)^{j+1}B_j(t). Indeed, apply alternatizeUncurryFin_apply to the tuple w := (x, u) ∈ E^{k+2} and split off the index 0 (`Fin.sum_univ_succ`): the index 0 contributes Dφ(tx)[x](removeNth 0 w) = Dφ(tx)[x](u) (removeNth 0 (Fin.cons x u) = tail (Fin.cons x u) = u), and the index j+1 contributes (−1)^{j+1}Dφ(tx)[u_j](removeNth (j+1) (Fin.cons x u)) with removeNth (j+1) (Fin.cons x u) = Fin.cons x (removeNth j u) (Mathlib `Fin.cons_comp_succ_succAbove`).
2. By the hypothesis on χ and Step 1: χ(x)(u) = ∫_0^1 ( t^{k+1}A(t) + Σ_j (−1)^{j+1}t^{k+1}B_j(t) ) dt.
3. (Expansion of dψ.) By alternatizeUncurryFin_apply and the hypothesis on Dψ (with w := u_j, v := û_j): dψ(x)(u) = Σ_j (−1)^j Dψ(x)[u_j](û_j) = Σ_j (−1)^j ∫_0^1 t^k( tB_j(t) + C_j(t) ) dt = ∫_0^1 Σ_j (−1)^j t^k( tB_j(t) + C_j(t) ) dt (`intervalIntegral.integral_const_mul`, `intervalIntegral.integral_finsetSum`).
4. (Alternating identity.) For every α ∈ Λ_{k+1}: Σ_{j=0}^{k} (−1)^j α(u_j, û_j) = (k+1)·α(u). This is Mathlib's `ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft` (alternatizeUncurryFin (curryLeft α) = (k+1)•α) evaluated at u, rewritten with alternatizeUncurryFin_apply and curryLeft_apply_apply. (Equivalently: (u_j, û_j) is u composed with a cycle of sign (−1)^j.) With α := φ(tx): Σ_j (−1)^jC_j(t) = (k+1)D(t).
5. (Combination.) Adding Steps 2 and 3 (`intervalIntegral.integral_add`), χ(x)(u) + dψ(x)(u) = ∫_0^1 I(t) dt with I(t) = t^{k+1}A(t) + Σ_j [(−1)^{j+1} + (−1)^j] t^{k+1}B_j(t) + t^k Σ_j (−1)^jC_j(t) = t^{k+1}A(t) + (k+1)t^kD(t), using Step 4.
6. (Fundamental theorem of calculus.) g(t) := t^{k+1}D(t) = t^{k+1}φ(tx)(u) has derivative g′(t) = (k+1)t^kD(t) + t^{k+1}A(t) (product rule; chain rule for t ↦ φ(t•x), whose derivative is Dφ(tx)[x]; evaluation at u is continuous linear), and g′ = I is continuous. By `intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt`, ∫_0^1 I(t) dt = g(1) − g(0) = φ(x)(u) − 0^{k+1}φ(0)(u) = φ(x)(u), because k + 1 ≥ 1.
7. Hence χ(x)(u) + dψ(x)(u) = φ(x)(u) for all u, i.e. χ(x) + dψ(x) = φ(x) (ext).

Part (b). Fix x ∈ E and let v be the unique element of E^0 = (Fin 0 → E).
8. dφ(tx)(x, v) = Σ_{i ∈ Fin 1}(−1)^i Dφ(tx)[w_i](removeNth i w) with w = (x, v) (`Fin.sum_univ_one`), which equals Dφ(tx)[x](removeNth 0 w) = Dφ(tx)[x](v), since Fin 0 → E is a subsingleton.
9. g(t) := φ(tx)(v) has the continuous derivative Dφ(tx)[x](v), so by the hypothesis on χ and the fundamental theorem of calculus, χ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 1·Dφ(tx)[x](v) dt = g(1) − g(0) = φ(x)(v) − φ(0)(v).
10. As v is the only element of Fin 0 → E, χ(x) = φ(x) − φ(0) (ext). ∎
proof_key_steps: Expand dφ(tx)(x, u) and dψ(x)(u) with alternatizeUncurryFin_apply, using removeNth 0 (x, u) = u and removeNth (j+1) (x, u) = (x, removeNth j u).
The cross terms t^{k+1}Dφ(tx)[u_j](x, û_j) cancel between χ(x)(u) and dψ(x)(u).
Σ_j (−1)^j α(u_j, û_j) = (k+1)α(u) (alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft), so the integrand becomes d/dt[t^{k+1}φ(tx)(u)].
The fundamental theorem of calculus on [0,1] gives φ(x)(u) − 0 = φ(x)(u) since k+1 ≥ 1; in degree 0 it gives φ(x) − φ(0).

subproblems.title: Supports of boundaries, weak limits and linear combinations
subproblems.statement: (1) For P, m ∈ ℕ, any U ⊆ ℝ^P and Z ∈ D_{m+1}(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U (m+1)): spt ∂Z ⊆ spt Z. (2) For P, n ∈ ℕ, open U ⊆ ℝ^P, closed K ⊆ ℝ^P and Z_j, Z ∈ D_n(U) with spt Z_j ⊆ K for all j and Z_j ⇀ Z: spt Z ⊆ K. (3) For P, n ∈ ℕ, open U ⊆ ℝ^P, Z_1, Z_2, Z ∈ D_n(U) and a, b ∈ ℝ with Z(ω) = a·Z_1(ω) + b·Z_2(ω) for all ω ∈ D^n(U): spt Z ⊆ spt Z_1 ∪ spt Z_2.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), Z.boundary.support ⊆ Z.support) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (K : Set (Eucl P)) (Zj : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n) (Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsClosed K → (∀ j, (Zj j).support ⊆ K) → WeaklyConvergesOn Zj Z → Z.support ⊆ K) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)), IsOpen U → ∀ (Z₁ Z₂ Z : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (a b : ℝ), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Z ω = a * Z₁ ω + b * Z₂ ω) → Z.support ⊆ Z₁.support ∪ Z₂.support)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the support facts used in Part II, Step 7 (spt ∂T_j ⊆ spt T_j, (F4) for weak limits) and Step 9 (spt T′_j ⊆ spt T_j ∪ spt C_j) of the parent proof, made explicit.

Recall spt Z = U ∖ zeroRegion(Z), where zeroRegion(Z) is the union of all W with W open, closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and Z(η) = 0 for every η ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport η ⊆ W (“Z vanishes on W”). (F2′): by the reused lemma isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support, Z(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ spt Z = ∅. (Balls): for x ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0, W := B_r(x) is open, closure W = B̄_r(x) (`closure_ball`) is compact (`isCompact_closedBall`); so W is admissible for zeroRegion as soon as B̄_r(x) ⊆ U and Z vanishes on W.

1. (Part (1).) Let x ∈ spt ∂Z, so x ∈ U, and suppose x ∉ spt Z. Then x ∈ zeroRegion(Z): x ∈ W for some W open with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, and Z vanishing on W. For φ ∈ D^m(U) with tsupport φ ⊆ W we have tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ ⊆ W (SimonGMT `tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset`), so ∂Z(φ) = Z(dφ) = 0. Thus ∂Z vanishes on W, W is admissible for zeroRegion(∂Z), and x ∈ zeroRegion(∂Z), contradicting x ∈ spt ∂Z. Hence spt ∂Z ⊆ spt Z. (No openness of U is needed.)
2. (Part (2).) Let x ∈ spt Z ⊆ U and suppose x ∉ K. The set U ∖ K is open (U open, K closed) and contains x, so there is r > 0 with B̄_r(x) ⊆ U ∖ K (take half of a radius of a ball inside U ∖ K). Let W := B_r(x). For ω ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W: tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅, hence tsupport ω ∩ spt Z_j = ∅ for every j, so Z_j(ω) = 0 by (F2′); since Z_j(ω) → Z(ω) and limits in ℝ are unique, Z(ω) = 0. So Z vanishes on W, W is admissible, x ∈ zeroRegion(Z), contradicting x ∈ spt Z. Hence spt Z ⊆ K.
3. (Part (3).) Let x ∈ spt Z ⊆ U and suppose x ∉ spt Z_1 ∪ spt Z_2. As x ∈ U, x ∈ zeroRegion(Z_1) ∩ zeroRegion(Z_2) ∩ U, an open set (zero regions are unions of open sets, U is open), so there is r > 0 with B̄_r(x) contained in it. Let W := B_r(x). For ω ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W: tsupport ω ⊆ zeroRegion(Z_i), which is disjoint from spt Z_i = U ∖ zeroRegion(Z_i), so Z_i(ω) = 0 by (F2′) (i = 1, 2), and Z(ω) = a·0 + b·0 = 0. So Z vanishes on W, W is admissible (B̄_r(x) ⊆ U), x ∈ zeroRegion(Z), contradicting x ∈ spt Z. Hence spt Z ⊆ spt Z_1 ∪ spt Z_2. ∎
proof_key_steps: If Z vanishes on an admissible W then so does ∂Z, because tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ; hence spt ∂Z ⊆ spt Z.
For x ∉ K a small ball W around x misses K, so every Z_j kills test forms supported in W (reused vanishing lemma) and so does the weak limit Z.
For x outside spt Z_1 ∪ spt Z_2 a small ball lies in both zero regions; both Z_i, hence Z = aZ_1 + bZ_2, vanish on it.

subproblems.title: Existence of the cone 0⨯X over a compactly supported current
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, R ∈ ℝ and X ∈ D_m(ℝ^P) with spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0). Then there is C ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P) (a cone 0⨯X over X) such that, for all ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) and ψ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P): if there is an open N ⊇ spt X with ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for all x ∈ N and v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m, then C(ω) = X(ψ). [Cone(X, C)]
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (R : ℝ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m), X.support ⊆ closedBall 0 R → ∃ C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1), (∀ (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) (m + 1)) (ψ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) m), (∃ N : Set (Eucl P), IsOpen N ∧ X.support ⊆ N ∧ ∀ x ∈ N, ∀ v : Fin m → Eucl P, (ψ : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) m) x v = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ m * (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) (m + 1)) (t • x) (Fin.cons x v)) → C ω = X ψ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P; D^k(ℝ^P) := TestFormOn univ k (C^∞ k-forms with compact tsupport); D_k(ℝ^P) := GeometricCurrentOn univ k; Λ_k := Covector (ℝ^P) k (continuous alternating k-linear forms) with Mathlib's operator norm ‖·‖; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α (the Euclidean coefficient norm used in the mass); (x, v) := Fin.cons x v for x ∈ ℝ^P, v ∈ (ℝ^P)^k; spt := support, M := mass, ⇀ := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary, d := extDeriv; B_r(0), B̄_r(0) are the open and closed balls. For ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P), ψ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P) and N ⊆ ℝ^P, say that ψ satisfies the Hω-formula on N if ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for all x ∈ N and all v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m. For X ∈ D_m(ℝ^P) and C ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P), Cone(X, C) means: for all ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) and ψ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P), if ψ satisfies the Hω-formula on some open N ⊇ spt X, then C(ω) = X(ψ). (This is verbatim the inline Lean predicate of the statement.) Bump functions: for 0 < r < s there is ζ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; ℝ) with 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, ζ = 1 on B̄_r(0) and tsupport ζ = B̄_s(0) (a Mathlib ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn = r, rOut = s); for such ζ and a C^∞ k-form ψ, ζψ := (x ↦ ζ(x)•ψ(x)) ∈ D^k(ℝ^P) (ContDiff.smul; tsupport(ζψ) ⊆ tsupport ζ, compact).

Source: Part I of the parent proof — definition (0⨯X)(ω) := X(ζ·Hω) with Hω(x) = ∫_0^1 t^m x⌟ω(tx) dt, ζ = 1 near spt X, its independence of ζ by (F2), and item 1 (0⨯X is linear and sequentially continuous) — filled in.

1. (Cut-off.) Let R₀ := max(R, 0), so spt X ⊆ B̄_{R₀}(0). Fix ζ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; ℝ) with ζ = 1 on B̄_{R₀+1}(0) and tsupport ζ = B̄_{R₀+2}(0) =: K′ (ContDiffBump at 0 with radii R₀+1 < R₀+2). K′ is compact, and Z_i := sup_x ‖D^iζ(x)‖ < ∞ for each i (D^iζ is continuous and vanishes off K′).
2. (Radial forms.) For ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P), ω is a C^∞ (m+1)-form, so iwl_cr_radial_operator (with P, k := m, a := m) gives a C^∞ m-form ψ_ω with (i) ψ_ω(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for all x, v, and (iii) the derivative bounds. By (i), ψ_ω(x) is determined for every x (a covector is determined by its values), so ψ_ω is uniquely determined by ω; fix this choice.
3. (Linearity.) For ω, ω′ ∈ D^{m+1} and c ∈ ℝ: ψ_{ω+ω′} = ψ_ω + ψ_{ω′} and ψ_{cω} = cψ_ω. Evaluate at (x, v) with (i) and use linearity of the interval integral; the integrands t ↦ t^m ω(tx)(x, v) are continuous, hence interval integrable on [0,1].
4. (The operator Φ.) Put Φ(ω) := ζψ_ω = (x ↦ ζ(x)•ψ_ω(x)). Then Φ(ω) ∈ D^m(ℝ^P): it is C^∞ (`ContDiff.smul`), and tsupport Φ(ω) ⊆ tsupport ζ = K′ (`tsupport_smul_subset_left`) is compact (and ⊆ univ). By Step 3, Φ : D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) → D^m(ℝ^P) is ℝ-linear.

Since support(D^iω_l) ⊆ tsupport ω_l ⊆ K (`support_iteratedFDeriv_subset`), δ_l^{(i)} := sup_{y ∈ ℝ^P}‖D^iω_l(y)‖ = sup_{y ∈ K}‖D^iω_l(y)‖ → 0 as l → ∞, for every i. Hence D^jΦ(ω_l) → 0 uniformly on K′, for every j; together with tsupport Φ(ω_l) ⊆ K′ for all l (and tsupport 0 = ∅), this is TestFormOnConverges (Φ ∘ ω) 0 with the compact set K′ ⊆ univ.
6. (The current.) Define C(ω) := X(Φ(ω)) for ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P). C is ℝ-linear (X and Φ are linear), and if TestFormOnConverges ω_l 0 then TestFormOnConverges Φ(ω_l) 0 by Step 5, so C(ω_l) = X(Φ(ω_l)) → 0 by X.continuous'. Thus C ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ (m+1).
7. (Cone property.) Let ω ∈ D^{m+1}, ψ ∈ D^m and N open with spt X ⊆ N such that ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for x ∈ N and all v. Put N′ := N ∩ B_{R₀+1}(0): it is open and contains spt X (spt X ⊆ B̄_{R₀}(0) ⊆ B_{R₀+1}(0)). For x ∈ N′, ζ(x) = 1, so Φ(ω)(x)(v) = ψ_ω(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt = ψ(x)(v) for all v, i.e. ψ(x) = Φ(ω)(x). Hence the test form ψ − Φ(ω) vanishes on the open set N′, so its support lies in the closed set ℝ^P ∖ N′ and therefore tsupport(ψ − Φ(ω)) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ N′, which is disjoint from spt X. By isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support and linearity, X(ψ) − X(Φ(ω)) = X(ψ − Φ(ω)) = 0, i.e. X(ψ) = C(ω). So Cone(X, C) holds. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix a bump ζ = 1 on B̄_{R₀+1}(0) with compact support; for each test form ω take the unique C^∞ radial form ψ_ω of iwl_cr_radial_operator (k = a = m).
Φ(ω) := ζψ_ω is a linear map D^{m+1} → D^m; the derivative bounds (iii) and the Leibniz rule give Φ(ω_l) → 0 in the test-form topology whenever ω_l → 0.
C(ω) := X(Φ(ω)) is therefore a linear, sequentially continuous current.
Any ψ satisfying the Hω-formula on an open N ⊇ spt X agrees with Φ(ω) on the open N ∩ B_{R₀+1}(0) ⊇ spt X, so X(ψ) = X(Φ(ω)) = C(ω) by the reused vanishing lemma.

Conventions. For X ∈ D_m(ℝ^P) and C ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P), Cone(X, C) means: for all ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) and ψ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P), if ψ satisfies the Hω-formula on some open N ⊇ spt X, then C(ω) = X(ψ). Bump functions: for 0 < r < s there is ζ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; ℝ) with 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, ζ = 1 on B̄_r(0) and tsupport ζ = B̄_s(0) (a Mathlib ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn = r, rOut = s); for such ζ and a C^∞ k-form ψ, ζψ := (x ↦ ζ(x)•ψ(x)) ∈ D^k(ℝ^P) (ContDiff.smul; tsupport(ζψ) ⊆ tsupport ζ, compact).

Source: Part I, items 3 (mass and support) and 4 (weak continuity) of the parent proof, filled in. The parent's pointwise bound |x⌟α| ≤ |x||α| (F3) is replaced by the cruder coefficient estimate of Step 4 below (constant P^{m+1}), which uses only the reused lemma isoperimetric_abs_covector_apply_le; only finiteness of the constant matters for the parent.

Take c := P^{2m+1} ≥ 0 and fix R ≥ 0.
0. (Notation.) For ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P), ψ_ω denotes the C^∞ m-form from iwl_cr_radial_operator (P, k := m, a := m): ψ_ω(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt. For 0 < r < s, ζ_{r,s} denotes a C^∞ function with 0 ≤ ζ_{r,s} ≤ 1, ζ_{r,s} = 1 on B̄_r(0) and tsupport ζ_{r,s} ⊆ B̄_s(0) (ContDiffBump). Then ζ_{r,s}ψ_ω ∈ D^m(ℝ^P) and it satisfies the Hω-formula on the open ball B_r(0).
1. (Evaluating cones.) If spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0), Cone(X, C) and R < r < s, then C(ω) = X(ζ_{r,s}ψ_ω) for every ω: apply Cone(X, C) with ψ := ζ_{r,s}ψ_ω and N := B_r(0) ⊇ B̄_R(0) ⊇ spt X.
Part (a).
2. (Vanishing away from the ball.) Let ω ∈ D^{m+1} with tsupport ω ∩ B̄_R(0) = ∅. The compact set B̄_R(0) lies in the open set ℝ^P ∖ tsupport ω, so there is δ > 0 with thickening δ (B̄_R(0)) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ tsupport ω (`IsCompact.exists_thickening_subset_open`), and B_{R+δ}(0) ⊆ thickening δ (B̄_R(0)) (if ‖y‖ < R + δ then dist(y, B̄_R(0)) ≤ max(‖y‖ − R, 0) < δ). Thus ψ := 0 satisfies the Hω-formula on the open N ⊇ B̄_R(0) ⊇ spt X, and Cone(X, C) gives C(ω) = X(0) = 0.
3. (Support.) Let p ∉ B̄_R(0) and r := (‖p‖ − R)/2 > 0. W := B_r(p) is open, closure W = B̄_r(p) is compact and ⊆ univ, and B̄_r(p) ∩ B̄_R(0) = ∅ (if ‖q − p‖ ≤ r then ‖q‖ ≥ ‖p‖ − r = R + r > R). If tsupport ω ⊆ W then tsupport ω ∩ B̄_R(0) = ∅, so C(ω) = 0 by Step 2. Thus C vanishes on W, W lies in the zero region of C, and p ∉ spt C. Hence spt C ⊆ B̄_R(0).
4. (Coefficient estimate.) Let α ∈ Λ_{m+1}, x ∈ ℝ^P and I : Fin m → Fin P, e_I := (e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(m)}). Then |α(x, e_I)| ≤ P^{m+1}‖x‖·|α|. For x = 0 the left side is 0 by multilinearity. For x ≠ 0, multilinearity in the first slot gives α(x, e_I) = ‖x‖·α(x/‖x‖, e_I), and every entry of τ := (x/‖x‖, e_I) has norm ≤ 1, so the reused lemma isoperimetric_abs_covector_apply_le gives |α(τ)| ≤ P^{m+1}|α|.
5. (Pointwise bound.) Assume |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. For x ∈ ℝ^P and every I : Fin m → Fin P, by Step 0 and Step 4, |ψ_ω(x)(e_I)| ≤ ∫_0^1 t^m|ω(tx)(x, e_I)| dt ≤ ∫_0^1 t^m P^{m+1}‖x‖ dt ≤ P^{m+1}‖x‖. |ψ_ω(x)| is the square root of a sum over the P^m maps I : Fin m → Fin P of terms that are 0 or ψ_ω(x)(e_I)², so |ψ_ω(x)| ≤ (P^m)^{1/2}·P^{m+1}‖x‖ ≤ P^{2m+1}‖x‖ = c‖x‖ (for P ≥ 1, (P^m)^{1/2} ≤ P^m; for P = 0 all terms vanish because P^{m+1} = 0). Also |sα| = |s|·|α| for s ∈ ℝ (each coefficient scales by s).
6. (Mass.) Assume M(X) < ∞ and put B := M(X).toReal ≥ 0, so M(X) = ofReal B. Let ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn univ (m+1) univ, i.e. |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y. For δ > 0 let ζ_δ := ζ_{R+δ/2, R+δ} and ψ := ζ_δψ_ω. By Step 1, C(ω) = X(ψ). For every x: if ‖x‖ > R + δ then ψ(x) = 0; otherwise |ψ(x)| = ζ_δ(x)|ψ_ω(x)| ≤ c‖x‖ ≤ c(R + δ) (Step 5). By the reused lemma cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le (U = W = univ, bound B, pointwise bound c(R+δ)), |X(ψ)| ≤ B·c(R + δ). Hence C(ω) ≤ Bc(R + δ) for every δ > 0, so C(ω) ≤ cR·B, and ofReal(C(ω)) ≤ ofReal(cR·B) = ofReal(cR)·ofReal(B) = ofReal(cR)·M(X) (`ENNReal.ofReal_mul`, cR ≥ 0). Part (b).
7. Let ω ∈ D^{m+1} and ψ := ζ_{R+1,R+2}ψ_ω. By Step 1 (applied to each pair (X_j, C_j) and to (X, C), whose supports lie in B̄_R(0)), C_j(ω) = X_j(ψ) and C(ω) = X(ψ). As X_j ⇀ X, X_j(ψ) → X(ψ), i.e. C_j(ω) → C(ω). Since ω is arbitrary, C_j ⇀ C. ∎
proof_key_steps: For R < r < s, C(ω) = X(ζ_{r,s}ψ_ω) by the cone property, with one test form valid for all currents supported in B̄_R(0).
If ω vanishes near B̄_R(0) then so does the radial integral, so C(ω) = X(0) = 0; hence spt C ⊆ B̄_R(0).
Coefficient estimate |α(x, e_I)| ≤ P^{m+1}‖x‖|α| (reused covector bound) gives |ζ_δψ_ω(x)| ≤ P^{2m+1}(R + δ) for admissible ω; the reused mass bound and δ ↓ 0 give M(C) ≤ P^{2m+1}R·M(X).
Weak continuity: C_j(ω) = X_j(ψ) → X(ψ) = C(ω) for the single test form ψ = ζ_{R+1,R+2}ψ_ω.

Source: Part I, item 2 of the parent proof (∂(0⨯X) = X for X = ∂Y with Y compactly supported, via the radial homotopy formula for m ≥ 1 and H(dφ) = φ − φ(0) for m = 0). The two cases are handled uniformly through dχ = dφ for χ := H(dφ), using (F2) for Y only.

1. (Set-up.) Let R₀ := max(R, 0), B := B_{R₀+1}(0) (open) and fix ζ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; ℝ) with ζ = 1 on B̄_{R₀+1}(0) and compact tsupport ζ ⊆ B̄_{R₀+2}(0) (ContDiffBump). Then spt Y ⊆ B̄_R(0) ⊆ B, and by iwl_cr_support_lemmas (1) (U = univ, Z = Y), spt ∂Y ⊆ spt Y ⊆ B.
2. Fix φ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P). Its exterior derivative dφ ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) (`exteriorDerivativeTestOn`; as a form it is extDeriv φ, which is C^∞). By definition of the boundary, ∂C(φ) = C(dφ) and ∂Y(φ) = Y(dφ).
3. (χ := H(dφ).) Apply iwl_cr_radial_operator to the C^∞ (m+1)-form dφ with k := m and a := m: there is a C^∞ m-form χ with χ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m dφ(tx)(x, v) dt for all x, v. Then ζχ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P), and since ζ = 1 on B, ζχ satisfies the Hω-formula for ω := dφ on the open set B ⊇ spt ∂Y. By Cone(∂Y, C): C(dφ) = ∂Y(ζχ) = Y(d(ζχ)).

 Case m = k + 1: apply iwl_cr_radial_operator to the C^∞ (k+1)-form φ with exponent a := k: there is a C^∞ k-form ψ with Dψ(x)[w](v) = ∫_0^1 t^k( t·(Dφ(tx)[w])(x, v) + φ(tx)(w, v) ) dt (formula (ii)). By Step 3, χ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^{k+1} dφ(tx)(x, v) dt. By iwl_cr_radial_homotopy (a), χ(x) + dψ(x) = φ(x) for all x, i.e. χ = φ − dψ. Since φ and dψ are C^∞ (ψ is C^∞), d(φ − dψ) = dφ − d(dψ) (there is no `extDeriv_sub`: use `extDeriv_add` with the differentiable forms φ and −dψ, and `extDeriv_smul` for the sign), and d(dψ) = 0 (`extDeriv_extDeriv`; ψ is C^∞, in particular C²). Hence dχ = dφ.
5. (Localization.) For x ∈ B, ζ = 1 on the neighbourhood B of x, so ζχ = χ on a neighbourhood of x; hence D(ζχ)(x) = Dχ(x) (`Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq`) and d(ζχ)(x) = dχ(x) = dφ(x).
6. So the test forms d(ζχ), dφ ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) agree on the open set B ⊇ spt Y. Their difference vanishes on B, so tsupport(d(ζχ) − dφ) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ B, which is disjoint from spt Y; by isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support and linearity, Y(d(ζχ)) = Y(dφ).

proof_key_steps: C(dφ) = ∂Y(ζχ) = Y(d(ζχ)) for χ := H(dφ) from iwl_cr_radial_operator, since ζχ satisfies the Hω-formula on B ⊇ spt ∂Y (support lemma (1)).
dχ = dφ: for m = 0, χ = φ − φ(0) (homotopy (b)); for m = k+1, χ = φ − d(H′φ) (homotopy (a) with H′φ from the radial operator, exponent k) and d² = 0.
d(ζχ) = dχ = dφ on the open ball B ⊇ spt Y, so Y(d(ζχ)) = Y(dφ) by the reused vanishing lemma.
Hence ∂C(φ) = Y(dφ) = ∂Y(φ) for every φ.

subproblems.title: Product formula for Hausdorff measure on ℝ × (countably rectifiable set)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ. Write Φ(s, x) := (s, x_1, …, x_P) ∈ ℝ^{P+1} for s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ ℝ^P (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))) and π(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) ∈ ℝ^P for y = (y_0, …, y_P) ∈ ℝ^{P+1} (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ y))), so {y : π(y) ∈ S} = Φ(ℝ × S). Hᵏ := μHE[k]. (a) If N ⊆ ℝ^P and H^m(N) = 0 then H^{m+1}({y : π(y) ∈ N}) = 0. (b) If A ⊆ ℝ^P is H^m-null-measurable, countably m-rectifiable and H^m(A ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K, then for every Borel g : ℝ^{P+1} → [0, ∞]: ∫⁻_{ {y : π(y) ∈ A} } g dH^{m+1} = ∫⁻_ℝ ∫⁻_A g(Φ(s, x)) dH^m(x) ds (product formula H^{m+1}⌞(ℝ × A) = L¹ ⊗ H^m⌞A, Federer 3.2.23).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P m : ℕ) (N : Set (Eucl P)), (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) N = 0 → (μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl (P + 1))) {y | (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ N} = 0) ∧ (∀ (P m : ℕ) (A : Set (Eucl P)), NullMeasurableSet A (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) → CountablyRectifiable m A → (∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → (μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)) (A ∩ K) < ∞) → ∀ g : Eucl (P + 1) → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g → ∫⁻ y in {y | (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ y)) ∈ A}, g y ∂(μHE[m + 1] : Measure (Eucl (P + 1))) = ∫⁻ s : ℝ, ∫⁻ x in A, g ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))) ∂(μHE[m] : Measure (Eucl P)))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is the product formula cited in Part I, item 5 of the parent proof: “H^{m+1}⌞((0,1) × M) = L¹⌞(0,1) ⊗ H^m⌞M (product formula for Hausdorff measure on rectifiable sets, Federer 3.2.23)” and “(0,1) × M_0 is H^{m+1}-null”. It is isolated as a named lemma and proved completely here.
- Part (a) is an elementary covering argument.
- Part (b) follows Federer's route to 3.2.23 (H. Federer, Geometric Measure Theory, 1969, 3.2.23; cf. its use in arXiv:2505.11279). Cut the Lipschitz parametrizations of A into injective Lipschitz pieces, apply the area formula for Lipschitz maps in dimensions m and m + 1, and use Tonelli.
- No C¹ chart cover is used, and no DAG declaration is needed (depends_on = []).
- The piece construction of Steps 6–7 is the one in the comparator-accepted proof of rectifiability_weighted_tangent_ae (node root.rectifiability-a1.weighted_tangent_ae-a1, Step 4(a)–(d) of its natural proof; Lean code in commit 2f36576, hypothesis `hpart`), specialized to dimension m.
- Every external input is a theorem of the pinned libraries (Library account below); each has #print axioms = [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

Library account (pinned Mathlib 25730c7c and SimonGMT 2b36630).
- (L1) Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn (simongmt Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter02/AreaLipschitz.lean:101).
  - Statement: let E, F be finite-dimensional real inner product spaces with Borel σ-algebras, f : E → F with LipschitzWith K f, s ⊆ E a MeasurableSet with InjOn f s, and g : F → [0, ∞] arbitrary (no measurability is needed). Then ∫⁻_{f '' s} g dμHE[finrank ℝ E] = ∫⁻_{x ∈ s} ENNReal.ofReal(J_f(x))·g(f(x)) dvolume(x).
  - Normalization: the target measure is Mathlib's normalized Hausdorff measure μHE. The source measure is Lebesgue measure volume. J_f(x) := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.areaJacobianAt f x = (fderiv ℝ f x).normDet (areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet), which is Simon's √det(Df(x)* Df(x)) of (3.3) (areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp). For E = Eucl k, finrank ℝ E = k (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), so the left side is the integral with respect to μHE[k].
  - Provenance: AreaLipschitz.lean derives (L1) from weighted_area_formula_volume_of_injective_derivative (Chapter02/WeightedArea.lean:120). That is the volume-normalized form of weighted_area_formula_of_injective_derivative (WeightedArea.lean:76), the area formula for maps that are injective on s with injective derivative at every point of s. The derivation discards the null images of the Rademacher exceptional set and of the critical set, so no rank or everywhere-differentiability hypothesis remains.
- (L2) Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.areaRegularSet f := {x | DifferentiableAt ℝ f x ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ f x)}. It is measurable (measurableSet_areaRegularSet, AreaLipschitz.lean:34). For Lipschitz f and every s, μHE[finrank ℝ E](f '' (s ∖ areaRegularSet f)) = 0 (area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero, AreaLipschitz.lean:59; Rademacher's theorem and the null critical image).
- (L3) Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.measurable_areaJacobianAt (Chapter02/AreaApproximation.lean:44): x ↦ J_f(x) is Borel.
- (L4) Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/Jacobian.lean:255), for f : E → F with E finite-dimensional and F second countable.
  - Input: hf′ : ∀ x ∈ s, HasFDerivWithinAt f (f′ x) s x, and r : (E →L[ℝ] F) → ℝ≥0 with r A ≠ 0.
  - Output: pairwise disjoint measurable t_n with s ⊆ ⋃_n t_n, and A_n with ApproximatesLinearOn f (A_n) (s ∩ t_n) (r(A_n)), i.e. ‖f x − f y − A_n(x − y)‖ ≤ r(A_n)‖x − y‖ on s ∩ t_n; moreover s.Nonempty → ∀ n, ∃ y ∈ s, A_n = f′ y.
- (L5) Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/Polish/Basic.lean:821): the image of a Borel subset of a Polish space under a map that is continuous and injective on it is Borel.
- (L6) Mathlib LinearMap.injective_iff_antilipschitz (Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/FiniteDimension.lean:242), and LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram (Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/NormDet.lean:303): normDet(L)² = det(⟨L b_i, L b_j⟩)_{i,j} for every orthonormal basis b of the source.
- (L7) Measure theory:
  - Sets and Hausdorff measures: NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq; Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def (μHE[k] = c_k • μH[k] with c_k := volume.addHaarScalarFactor μH[k] ∈ ℝ≥0, nonzero by addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero, hence 0 < c_k < ∞); Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero (μHE[0] = μH[0]); Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton (μH[0]{x} = 1); Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply (the δ-cover formula for μH[d]).
  - Integrals: lintegral_prod; Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'; lintegral_iUnion; lintegral_tsum; setLIntegral_congr.
  - Volume: measurePreserving_piFinSuccAbove; PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp; PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp.

Conventions.
- E := ℝ^P = Eucl P, E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P+1), and Hᵏ := μHE[k] on the relevant space. vol denotes Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ and on Eucl k.
- For s ∈ ℝ and x ∈ E, Φ(s,x) := (s, x_1, …, x_P) ∈ E′ (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P+1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x))). For y ∈ E′, y_0 is its 0-th coordinate and π(y) := (y_1, …, y_P) ∈ E (Lean as in the statement).
- Then π(Φ(s,x)) = x, y = Φ(y_0, π(y)), and ⟨Φ(s,x), Φ(s′,x′)⟩ = ss′ + ⟨x, x′⟩. In particular ‖Φ(s,x) − Φ(s′,x′)‖² = (s − s′)² + ‖x − x′‖².
- For S ⊆ E write Ŝ := {y : π(y) ∈ S} = Φ(ℝ × S). The map S ↦ Ŝ commutes with unions, intersections and differences, and Ŝ is Borel when S is (π is continuous linear).
- By (L7), μHE[k] and μH[k] have the same null sets.

Part (a). Let N ⊆ E with H^m(N) = 0. We show H^{m+1}(N̂) = 0.
1. (m = 0.) μHE[0] = μH[0] and μH[0]({x}) = 1 for every x (L7). So H^0(N) = 0 forces N = ∅, and then N̂ = ∅.
2. (m ≥ 1: what suffices.) N̂ = ⋃_{a ∈ ℤ} Φ([a, a+1] × N), so by countable subadditivity it suffices to show μH[m+1](Φ([a, a+1] × N)) = 0 for each a ∈ ℤ.
   - By hausdorffMeasure_apply, μH[m+1](S) = sup_{r>0} inf Σ_n diam(t_n)^{m+1}, the infimum over countable covers (t_n) of S with diam t_n ≤ r. (For m + 1 ≥ 1 the factor ⨆_{t_n ≠ ∅} is harmless because diam ∅ = 0.)
   - So it suffices: for every r > 0 and ε′ > 0, Φ([a, a+1] × N) has a countable cover by sets of diameter ≤ r with Σ diam^{m+1} ≤ ε′.
   - Given r, fix δ ∈ (0, 1) with √2·δ ≤ r. Steps 3–4 produce, for every ε ∈ (0, (δ/2)^m), such a cover with diameters ≤ √2·δ and Σ diam^{m+1} ≤ 2^{2+(m+1)/2}·ε.
3. (Covering N.) Since μH[m](N) = 0, the infimum in hausdorffMeasure_apply for the radius δ/2 is 0. So there are sets C_i (i ∈ ℕ) with N ⊆ ⋃_i C_i, diam C_i ≤ δ/2 and Σ_i (diam C_i)^m < ε. (Because m ≥ 1, (diam ∅)^m = 0^m = 0, so the factor ⨆_{C_i ≠ ∅} can be dropped. All diameters here are finite, so ediam = diam.)
   - Put d_i := max(diam C_i, (ε·2^{−i−1})^{1/m}).
   - Then 0 < d_i ≤ max(δ/2, ε^{1/m}) < δ < 1, and d_i^m ≤ (diam C_i)^m + ε·2^{−i−1}, so Σ_i d_i^m < 2ε.
4. (Covering the strip.) Let k_i := ⌈1/d_i⌉ ≤ 1/d_i + 1 ≤ 2/d_i.
   - [a, a+1] ⊆ ⋃_{k=0}^{k_i−1} [a + k·d_i, a + (k+1)·d_i], so Φ([a, a+1] × C_i) ⊆ ⋃_{k<k_i} Q_{i,k} with Q_{i,k} := Φ([a + k·d_i, a + (k+1)·d_i] × C_i).
   - By the distance formula, diam Q_{i,k} ≤ √(d_i² + (diam C_i)²) ≤ √2·d_i < √2·δ.
   - The countable family (Q_{i,k}) covers Φ([a, a+1] × N), and Σ_{i,k} (diam Q_{i,k})^{m+1} ≤ Σ_i (2/d_i)(√2·d_i)^{m+1} = 2^{1+(m+1)/2}·Σ_i d_i^m ≤ 2^{2+(m+1)/2}·ε.
   - To apply hausdorffMeasure_apply, index the family by ℕ: send n to Q_{i,k} if n = Nat.pair i k with k < k_i, and to ∅ otherwise. Empty sets contribute 0 because of the factor ⨆_{t_n ≠ ∅}.
   - By Step 2, μH[m+1](Φ([a, a+1] × N)) = 0 for every a, hence H^{m+1}(N̂) = 0.

Part (b). Let A be as in (b) and g : E′ → [0, ∞] measurable.
For B ⊆ E and s ∈ ℝ write:
- LHS(B) := ∫⁻_{B̂} g dH^{m+1};
- φ_B(s) := ∫⁻_{x ∈ B} g(Φ(s,x)) dH^m(x);
- RHS(B) := ∫⁻_ℝ φ_B(s) ds.
The goal is LHS(A) = RHS(A). The function (s, x) ↦ g(Φ(s,x)) is Borel on ℝ × E (Φ is continuous).

5. (Reduction to Borel A.) By NullMeasurableSet.exists_measurable_subset_ae_eq there is a Borel A₀ ⊆ A with H^m(A ∖ A₀) = 0.
   - Â = Â₀ ∪ (A ∖ A₀)^, and H^{m+1}((A ∖ A₀)^) = 0 by Part (a). So Â =ᵐ Â₀ for H^{m+1}, and LHS(A) = LHS(A₀) (setLIntegral_congr).
   - For every s, A =ᵐ A₀ for H^m, so φ_A(s) = φ_{A₀}(s) and RHS(A) = RHS(A₀).
   - A₀ is countably m-rectifiable (CountablyRectifiable.mono) and H^m(A₀ ∩ K) ≤ H^m(A ∩ K) < ∞ for compact K.
   - So we may and do assume that A is Borel.
   - Then H^m⌞A is σ-finite: E = ⋃_k B̄_k(0) and H^m(A ∩ B̄_k(0)) < ∞. Hence H^m⌞A′ is σ-finite (in particular s-finite) for every Borel A′ ⊆ A.
6. (Injective Lipschitz pieces.) By CountablyRectifiable m A, A ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_i F_i(Eucl m) with H^m(M₀) = 0 and F_i : Eucl m → E satisfying LipschitzWith K_i F_i.
   - Fix i and let R_i := areaRegularSet F_i, which is Borel by (L2). For b ∈ R_i, F_i has Fréchet derivative fderiv ℝ F_i b at b, hence HasFDerivWithinAt F_i (fderiv ℝ F_i b) R_i b.
   - For each injective continuous linear L : Eucl m → E, fix by (L6) a constant c_L > 0 with ‖Lv‖ ≥ c_L‖v‖ for all v, and put r(L) := c_L/2. Put r(L) := 1 if L is not injective. Then r(L) ≠ 0 for all L.
   - Apply (L4) to F_i, s := R_i, f′ := fderiv ℝ F_i and r. This gives pairwise disjoint Borel sets t_{i,l} (l ∈ ℕ) with R_i ⊆ ⋃_l t_{i,l}, and continuous linear maps A_{i,l}, with the following properties.
     - Put S_{i,l} := R_i ∩ t_{i,l} (Borel). Then ‖F_i(b) − F_i(b′) − A_{i,l}(b − b′)‖ ≤ r(A_{i,l})·‖b − b′‖ for b, b′ ∈ S_{i,l}.
     - If R_i ≠ ∅, then A_{i,l} = fderiv ℝ F_i y for some y ∈ R_i, which is injective by the definition of R_i.
   - Hence, if S_{i,l} ≠ ∅, A_{i,l} is injective and, with c := c_{A_{i,l}} > 0, for b, b′ ∈ S_{i,l}: ‖F_i(b) − F_i(b′)‖ ≥ ‖A_{i,l}(b − b′)‖ − (c/2)‖b − b′‖ ≥ (c/2)‖b − b′‖. So F_i is injective on S_{i,l} (trivially also if S_{i,l} = ∅).
   - Enumerate the pairs (i, l) by p ∈ ℕ via (i, l) = Nat.unpair p, and write G_p := F_i and S_p := S_{i,l}. Then:
     - G_p is LipschitzWith K_i and S_p is Borel;
     - G_p is injective on S_p and differentiable at every point of S_p (S_p ⊆ R_i);
     - G_p '' S_p is Borel by (L5) (Eucl m is Polish and G_p is continuous).
   - Let N := M₀ ∪ ⋃_i F_i '' (Eucl m ∖ R_i). Then H^m(N) = 0 by (L2) (with s := Eucl m and finrank ℝ (Eucl m) = m) and countable subadditivity.
   - A ⊆ N ∪ ⋃_p G_p '' S_p. Indeed, if x ∈ A ∖ M₀, then x = F_i(b) for some i and b. If b ∉ R_i then x ∈ N. Otherwise b ∈ t_{i,l} for some l, so x ∈ G_p '' S_p for the index p of (i, l).
7. (Disjoint pieces.) Put A_p := (A ∩ G_p '' S_p) ∖ ⋃_{q<p} G_q '' S_q and B_p := S_p ∩ G_p⁻¹(A_p).
   - Both are Borel (Step 5, Step 6, continuity of G_p).
   - The A_p are pairwise disjoint subsets of A.
   - A ∖ ⋃_p A_p ⊆ N: if x ∈ A ∖ N, let p be the least index with x ∈ G_p '' S_p; then x ∈ A_p.
   - G_p maps B_p bijectively onto A_p, because A_p ⊆ G_p '' S_p and G_p is injective on S_p ⊇ B_p.
8. (Area formula in dimension m.) For each p and every function u : E → [0, ∞], (L1) with f := G_p and s := B_p (measurable, InjOn, G_p '' B_p = A_p) gives
   ∫⁻_{A_p} u dH^m = ∫⁻_{b ∈ B_p} J_p(b)·u(G_p(b)) db, where J_p(b) := ENNReal.ofReal(areaJacobianAt G_p b).   (8.1)
9. (The lifted pieces.) For w ∈ Eucl (m+1), let w_0 be its 0-th coordinate and tl(w) ∈ Eucl m its remaining coordinates (Lean: (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin m) ℝ).symm (Fin.tail (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (m+1)) ℝ w))). Then ‖w − w′‖² = (w_0 − w′_0)² + ‖tl w − tl w′‖².
   Define G̃_p : Eucl (m+1) → E′ by G̃_p(w) := Φ(w_0, G_p(tl w)), and B̃_p := {w : tl w ∈ B_p} (Borel).
   (i) G̃_p is Lipschitz: ‖G̃_p(w) − G̃_p(w′)‖² = (w_0 − w′_0)² + ‖G_p(tl w) − G_p(tl w′)‖² ≤ max(1, K_i)²·‖w − w′‖².
   (ii) G̃_p is injective on B̃_p. If G̃_p(w) = G̃_p(w′), then w_0 = w′_0 and G_p(tl w) = G_p(tl w′). Hence tl w = tl w′, as both lie in B_p ⊆ S_p, and so w = w′.
   (iii) G̃_p '' B̃_p = Â_p.
       - For w ∈ B̃_p, π(G̃_p(w)) = G_p(tl w) ∈ A_p.
       - Conversely, if π(y) ∈ A_p, then π(y) = G_p(b) with b ∈ B_p. The w with w_0 = y_0 and tl w = b satisfies G̃_p(w) = Φ(y_0, π(y)) = y.
   (iv) (Jacobian.) Let w ∈ B̃_p, b := tl w ∈ S_p and L := fderiv ℝ G_p b (G_p is differentiable at b). We show areaJacobianAt G̃_p w = areaJacobianAt G_p (tl w), so J̃_p(w) = J_p(tl w) on B̃_p.
       - By the chain rule G̃_p is differentiable at w with derivative L̃(ω) = ω_0·Φ(1,0) + Φ(0, L(tl ω)).
       - Let (e_0, …, e_m) and (e′_0, …, e′_{m−1}) be the standard orthonormal bases of Eucl (m+1) and Eucl m (0-based, as in Lean's Fin). Then L̃e_0 = Φ(1,0) and L̃e_{j+1} = Φ(0, L e′_j) for 0 ≤ j < m, since (e_{j+1})_0 = 0 and tl e_{j+1} = e′_j (Lean: tl (single j.succ 1) = single j 1).
       - Since ‖Φ(1,0)‖ = 1, ⟨Φ(1,0), Φ(0,v)⟩ = 0 and ⟨Φ(0,u), Φ(0,v)⟩ = ⟨u, v⟩, the Gram matrix (⟨L̃e_i, L̃e_j⟩)_{0≤i,j≤m} has first row and column (1, 0, …, 0). Its entry at (i+1, j+1) is ⟨Le′_i, Le′_j⟩.
       - Expanding along the first row (Matrix.det_succ_row_zero), its determinant is det(⟨Le′_i, Le′_j⟩)_{0≤i,j<m}.
       - By (L6) and areaJacobianAt = normDet ∘ fderiv, (areaJacobianAt G̃_p w)² = (areaJacobianAt G_p b)². Both are ≥ 0, so they are equal.
       - For m = 0 both sides equal 1: the Gram matrices are (1) and the empty matrix.
10. (Area formula in dimension m+1, then Tonelli.) Fix p.
   - By (L1) with f := G̃_p and s := B̃_p (finrank ℝ (Eucl (m+1)) = m+1), using 9(i)–(iv):
     LHS(A_p) = ∫⁻_{Â_p} g dH^{m+1} = ∫⁻_{w ∈ B̃_p} J_p(tl w)·g(Φ(w_0, G_p(tl w))) dw.
   - Ψ(w) := (w_0, tl w) is measure preserving from vol on Eucl (m+1) to vol ⊗ vol on ℝ × Eucl m. It is the composite of PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp, measurePreserving_piFinSuccAbove at index 0, and PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp on the second factor. Moreover B̃_p = Ψ⁻¹(ℝ × B_p).
   - The function h(s, b) := 1_{B_p}(b)·J_p(b)·g(Φ(s, G_p(b))) is Borel on ℝ × Eucl m, by (L3), Borel g, and continuity of Φ and G_p.
   - The change of variables along Ψ, Tonelli (lintegral_prod) and (8.1) give
     LHS(A_p) = ∫⁻ h d(vol ⊗ vol) = ∫⁻_ℝ ∫⁻_{b ∈ B_p} J_p(b)·g(Φ(s, G_p(b))) db ds = ∫⁻_ℝ φ_{A_p}(s) ds = RHS(A_p).
     The third equality is (8.1) applied, for each fixed s, to u := g(Φ(s, ·)).
11. (Summation.)
   - The sets Â_p are Borel and pairwise disjoint, and ⋃_p Â_p ⊆ Â. Moreover Â ∖ ⋃_p Â_p = (A ∖ ⋃_p A_p)^ ⊆ N̂, which is H^{m+1}-null by Part (a). Hence, by setLIntegral_congr and lintegral_iUnion, LHS(A) = Σ_p LHS(A_p).
   - For every s, A =ᵐ ⋃_p A_p for H^m (the difference lies in N), so φ_A(s) = Σ_p φ_{A_p}(s).
   - Each φ_{A_p} is measurable by Measurable.lintegral_prod_right', applied to the Borel function (s, x) ↦ g(Φ(s,x)) and the s-finite measure H^m⌞A_p (Step 5). So lintegral_tsum gives RHS(A) = Σ_p RHS(A_p).
   - By Step 10, LHS(A) = Σ_p LHS(A_p) = Σ_p RHS(A_p) = RHS(A). ∎

Source: Part I, item 5, first paragraph of the parent proof (“the product current Π := [[(0,1)]] × X … If X = τ(M,θ,ξ) is i.m., then Π = τ((0,1) × M, θ∘π_2, e_0 ∧ ξ∘π_2) is i.m. (Simon 3.2(2)) … product formula for Hausdorff measure on rectifiable sets, Federer 3.2.23 … blow-ups of the product are products of blow-ups”), filled in. Here Π is defined directly as the τ-current of the product triple, and the parent's defining formula Π(η) = ∫_0^1 X(α_η(t,·)) dt is the slice formula proved in Step 5.

Conventions. E := ℝ^P, E′ := ℝ^{P+1}, Hᵏ := μHE[k] on the relevant space. Φ : ℝ × E → E′ as in the statement is a linear isometric isomorphism (‖Φ(s,x)‖² = s² + ‖x‖²), so it maps Hausdorff measures to Hausdorff measures (`Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`). e_0 := Φ(1,0), ι(v) := Φ(0,v) (a linear isometric embedding E → E′), π : E′ → E the linear 1-Lipschitz map with π(Φ(s,x)) = x. ℒ : Λ_{m+1}(E′) → Λ_m(E), ℒ(α)(v) := α(e_0, ιv_1, …, ιv_m), i.e. ℒ(α) = (α.curryLeft e_0).compContinuousLinearMap ι, is continuous linear with ‖ℒ‖ ≤ 1. The hypothesis on φ says φ(s)(x) = ℒ(η(Φ(s,x))) for s ∈ [0,1].
Write X = τ(M, θ, ξ): IsRectifiableTriple univ m M θ ξ, θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M (so θ ≥ 1 on M), and X(φ) = ∫_M θ ξ(φ) dH^m for all φ ∈ D^m(E). As θ ≥ 1 on M and θ is integrable on M ∩ K for compact K, H^m(M ∩ K) < ∞; so H^m⌞M is locally finite (σ-finite). Let G ⊆ M be the set of x for which there is an orthonormal τ = τ(x) ∈ E^m with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt m M θ x (span τ) and ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ; H^m(M ∖ G) = 0. For x ∈ G and α ∈ Λ_m(E), |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖.

1. (Product formula.) By iwl_cr_hausdorff_product_formula: (PF-null) if N ⊆ E and H^m(N) = 0 then H^{m+1}(Φ(ℝ × N)) = 0 (note {y : π(y) ∈ N} = Φ(ℝ × N)); (PF) if A ⊆ E is H^m-null-measurable, countably m-rectifiable and H^m(A ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K, then ∫_{Φ(ℝ×A)} g dH^{m+1} = ∫_ℝ ∫_A g(Φ(s, x)) dH^m(x) ds for every Borel g : E′ → [0, ∞]. (PF) extends to every g that is integrable on Φ(ℝ × A) (split g = g⁺ − g⁻) and to functions of the form g = (g₁ ∘ π)·g₂ with g₂ Borel and g₁ equal H^m⌞A-a.e. to a Borel function: changing g₁ on an H^m-null set N changes g only on Φ(ℝ × N), which is H^{m+1}-null by (PF-null) and does not affect the right-hand side. All sets to which (PF) is applied below (M, the blow-ups M_r, the plane T) satisfy its hypotheses.
2. (The product triple.) Put M̃ := Φ((0,1) × M), θ̃ := θ ∘ π and ξ̃(y) := ξ(π y) ∘L ℒ ∈ NVector E′ (m+1), so ξ̃(Φ(s,x))(α) = ξ(x)(ℒα). We verify IsRectifiableTriple univ (m+1) M̃ θ̃ ξ̃:
 (a) M̃ ⊆ univ.
 (b) Null-measurability: there is a Borel M_B with H^m(M Δ M_B) = 0; Φ((0,1) × M_B) is Borel (Φ is a homeomorphism) and M̃ Δ Φ((0,1) × M_B) ⊆ Φ(ℝ × (M Δ M_B)), which is H^{m+1}-null by (PF-null).
 (c) Countable (m+1)-rectifiability: M ⊆ M_0 ∪ ⋃_j range F_j with H^m(M_0) = 0 and F_j : Eucl m → E Lipschitz; hence M̃ ⊆ Φ(ℝ × M_0) ∪ ⋃_j range G_j with G_j : Eucl (m+1) → E′, G_j(u) := Φ(u_0, F_j(u_1, …, u_m)) Lipschitz, and H^{m+1}(Φ(ℝ × M_0)) = 0 by (PF-null).
 (d) For y = Φ(s,x) ∈ M̃: θ̃(y) = θ(x) > 0 and θ̃(y) ∈ ℕ.
 (e) Local integrability: a compact K′ ⊆ E′ satisfies M̃ ∩ K′ ⊆ Φ((0,1) × (M ∩ π(K′))) with π(K′) compact; by (PF) for A := M, ∫_{M̃ ∩ K′} θ̃ dH^{m+1} ≤ ∫_0^1 ∫_{M ∩ π(K′)} θ dH^m ds < ∞ (θ̃ is H^{m+1}⌞M̃-measurable after modification on the null set of (f)).
 (f) Measurability of ξ̃: ξ = ξ′ H^m-a.e. on M for a strongly measurable ξ′; ξ̃′(y) := ξ′(π y) ∘L ℒ is strongly measurable, and ξ̃ = ξ̃′ off Φ(ℝ × (M ∩ {ξ ≠ ξ′})), an H^{m+1}-null set by (PF-null). The same argument applies to θ̃.
 (g) Orientation: for y = Φ(s,x) with s ∈ (0,1), x ∈ G, let τ̃ := (e_0, ιτ_1, …, ιτ_m): it is orthonormal and Q := span τ̃ = Φ(ℝ × span τ). For α ∈ Λ_{m+1}(E′), ξ̃(y)(α) = ξ(x)(ℒα) = ±(ℒα)(τ) = ±α(τ̃), so ξ̃(y) = ±simpleNVector τ̃; the weighted tangent condition at y is Step 3. The exceptional set M̃ ∖ Φ((0,1) × G) ⊆ Φ(ℝ × (M ∖ G)) is H^{m+1}-null by (PF-null).
3. (Tangent planes of the product.) Fix y = Φ(s₀, x) with s₀ ∈ (0,1) and x ∈ G; T := span τ(x), Q := Φ(ℝ × T), finrank Q = m + 1. Let f ∈ C_c(E′) with spt f ⊆ Φ([−ρ, ρ] × B̄_ρ(0)). For r > 0: blowUpMap y r '' M̃ = Φ(I_r × M_r) with I_r := ((0,1) − s₀)/r and M_r := blowUpMap x r '' M (Φ is linear), and θ̃(y + rΦ(σ, w)) = θ(x + rw). M_r is H^m-null-measurable and countably m-rectifiable with H^m⌞M_r locally finite (M_r is the image of M under a similarity; `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image`). By (PF) for A := M_r (applied to the positive and negative parts of the integrand). All integrals here are finite: f is bounded with compact support, and ∫_{M_r ∩ B̄_ρ(0)} θ(x + rw) dH^m(w) = r^{−m}∫_{M ∩ B̄_{rρ}(x)} θ dH^m < ∞ by the scaling of Hausdorff measure under the homothety w ↦ x + rw (`euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image`) and the local integrability of θ. Thus:
 A(r) := ∫_{blowUpMap y r '' M̃} f(z) θ̃(y + rz) dH^{m+1}(z) = ∫_{I_r} a_r(σ) dσ, a_r(σ) := ∫_{M_r} f(Φ(σ, w)) θ(x + rw) dH^m(w).
 For each σ, f_σ := f(Φ(σ, ·)) ∈ C_c(E), so by the tangent property of (M, θ) at x, a_r(σ) → θ(x)∫_T f_σ dH^m as r → 0⁺. Fix g₀ ∈ C_c(E) with 0 ≤ g₀ ≤ 1 and g₀ = 1 on B̄_ρ(0); then |a_r(σ)| ≤ ‖f‖_∞ ∫_{M_r} g₀(w)θ(x + rw) dH^m(w) → ‖f‖_∞ θ(x)∫_T g₀, so there are r₀ > 0 and K₀ with |a_r(σ)| ≤ K₀ for 0 < r < r₀ and all σ, while a_r(σ) = 0 for |σ| > ρ. Since 0 < s₀ < 1, 1_{I_r}(σ) → 1 for every σ. Dominated convergence along r → 0⁺ (dominating function K₀·1_{[−ρ,ρ]}; `MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence`) gives A(r) → θ(x)∫_ℝ ∫_T f(Φ(σ, w)) dH^m(w) dσ = θ(x)∫_Q f dH^{m+1}, the last equality by (PF) for A := T (equivalently: μHE[m+1] restricted to the (m+1)-plane Q is its Lebesgue measure, `InnerProductSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`, and Φ|ℝ×T is a linear isometry onto Q). Since θ̃(y) = θ(x), this is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt (m+1) M̃ θ̃ y Q.
4. (The current Z.) For η ∈ D^{m+1}(E′) put Z(η) := tauAction (m+1) M̃ θ̃ ξ̃ η = ∫_{M̃} θ̃ ξ̃(η) dH^{m+1}. For H^{m+1}-a.e. y ∈ M̃ (by 2(g)), |ξ̃(y)(η(y))| = |η(y)(τ̃)| ≤ ‖η(y)‖ ≤ (sup‖η‖)·1_{tsupport η}(y), and θ̃ is integrable on M̃ ∩ tsupport η by 2(e); so the integrand is integrable and Z is ℝ-linear. If TestFormOnConverges η_l 0 (common compact support K′, sup‖η_l‖ → 0 by uniform convergence of the 0-th derivatives), then |Z(η_l)| ≤ (sup‖η_l‖)·∫_{M̃∩K′} θ̃ dH^{m+1} → 0. Hence Z ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ (m+1) on E′, and by Step 2 and 2(d), IsIntegerMultiplicity Z (triple (M̃, θ̃, ξ̃), θ̃ natural-valued on M̃, Z = tauAction).
5. (Slice formula.) Let η ∈ D^{m+1}(E′) and φ : ℝ → D^m(E) with φ(s)(x) = ℒ(η(Φ(s,x))) for s ∈ [0,1]. The integrand g := 1_{Φ((0,1)×ℝ^P)}·θ̃·ξ̃(η) is integrable on M̃ (Step 4) and is a finite sum of functions of the form covered by Step 1: fix a basis (b_l) of the finite-dimensional space Λ_m(E) with coordinate functionals (b*_l), so that α = Σ_l b*_l(α)·b_l for every α; then θ̃(y)ξ̃(y)(η(y)) = Σ_l (θ·ξ(·)(b_l))(π y)·b*_l(ℒη(y)), where each g₁ := θ·ξ(·)(b_l) is H^m⌞M-a.e. equal to a Borel function (θ and ξ are a.e.-measurable) and each g₂(y) := 1_{(0,1)}(y_0)·b*_l(ℒη(y)) is Borel (η is continuous). So, by (PF) for A := M applied to g (term by term, positive and negative parts), and Fubini for L¹⌞(0,1) ⊗ H^m⌞M (σ-finite): Z(η) = ∫_0^1 ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(ℒ(η(Φ(s,x)))) dH^m(x) ds = ∫_0^1 ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(φ(s)(x)) dH^m(x) ds = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds, because X(φ(s)) = tauAction m M θ ξ (φ(s)) for every s and the interval integral over [0,1] equals the integral over (0,1). ∎
proof_key_steps: Use the product formula H^{m+1}⌞Φ(ℝ × A) = L¹ ⊗ H^m⌞A and its null-set version from iwl_cr_hausdorff_product_formula (extended to a.e.-Borel integrands by (PF-null)).
The product triple (Φ((0,1)×M), θ∘π, ξ(π·)∘ℒ) is null-measurable, countably (m+1)-rectifiable, positive integer valued and locally integrable, with ξ̃ = ±simpleNVector(e_0, ιτ).
Blow-ups of the product are products of blow-ups: dominated convergence in the interval variable gives the weighted tangent plane ℝe_0 ⊕ ιT_x at a.e. point.
Z := τ(M̃, θ̃, ξ̃) is a current (integrable, sequentially continuous) and integer multiplicity; the product formula and Fubini give Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds.

Conventions. ℝ^P := Eucl P with standard orthonormal basis e_1,…,e_P; D^k(ℝ^P) := TestFormOn univ k (C^∞ k-forms with compact tsupport); D_k(ℝ^P) := GeometricCurrentOn univ k; Λ_k := Covector (ℝ^P) k (continuous alternating k-linear forms) with Mathlib's operator norm ‖·‖; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α (the Euclidean coefficient norm used in the mass); (x, v) := Fin.cons x v for x ∈ ℝ^P, v ∈ (ℝ^P)^k; spt := support, M := mass, ⇀ := WeaklyConvergesOn, ∂ := boundary, d := extDeriv; B_r(0), B̄_r(0) are the open and closed balls. For ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P), ψ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P) and N ⊆ ℝ^P, say that ψ satisfies the Hω-formula on N if ψ(x)(v) = ∫_0^1 t^m ω(tx)(x, v) dt for all x ∈ N and all v ∈ (ℝ^P)^m. For X ∈ D_m(ℝ^P) and C ∈ D_{m+1}(ℝ^P), Cone(X, C) means: for all ω ∈ D^{m+1}(ℝ^P) and ψ ∈ D^m(ℝ^P), if ψ satisfies the Hω-formula on some open N ⊇ spt X, then C(ω) = X(ψ). (This is verbatim the inline Lean predicate of the statement.) Bump functions: for 0 < r < s there is ζ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; ℝ) with 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, ζ = 1 on B̄_r(0) and tsupport ζ = B̄_s(0) (a Mathlib ContDiffBump centred at 0 with rIn = r, rOut = s); for such ζ and a C^∞ k-form ψ, ζψ := (x ↦ ζ(x)•ψ(x)) ∈ D^k(ℝ^P) (ContDiff.smul; tsupport(ζψ) ⊆ tsupport ζ, compact).

Source: Part I, item 5, second paragraph of the parent proof (push the product [[(0,1)]] × X forward by h(t,x) = tx with the sibling smooth push-forward; α_{h^#ω}(t,x) = t^m(x⌟ω(tx)); S(ω) = ∫_0^1 X(ζ t^m(·⌟ω(t·))) dt = X(ζHω) = (0⨯X)(ω)), filled in. The hypothesis H_push is exactly what the parent obtains from the sibling iwl_smooth_pushforward (with LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity, U := ℝ^{P+1}, V := ℝ^P, k := m), keeping only the integrality and the test-form identity. The exchange of X and ∫_0^1 dt is done by Fubini on the representation X = τ(M,θ,ξ) instead of Riemann sums.

Notation: E := ℝ^P, E′ := ℝ^{P+1}; Φ, e_0, ι, π and ℒ are as in iwl_cr_interval_product_im (Φ(s,x) = (s, x_1, …, x_P), e_0 = Φ(1,0), ι(v) = Φ(0,v), π(Φ(s,x)) = x, ℒ(α)(v) = α(e_0, ιv)). Let R₀ := max(R, 0), so spt X ⊆ B̄_{R₀}(0). Write X = τ(M, θ, ξ) (IsIntegerMultiplicity X); then H^m(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^m < ∞ for compact K (θ ≥ 1 on M), and |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for H^m-a.e. x ∈ M (ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector of an orthonormal frame).
1. (The product.) By iwl_cr_interval_product_im there is an integer multiplicity Z ∈ D_{m+1}(E′) with Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds for all η ∈ D^{m+1}(E′) and all φ : ℝ → D^m(E) with φ(s)(x)(v) = η(Φ(s,x))(e_0, ιv) for s ∈ [0,1].
2. (Slices.) For η ∈ D^{m+1}(E′) and s ∈ ℝ, η^♭_s(x) := ℒ(η(Φ(s,x))) defines η^♭_s ∈ D^m(E): it is C^∞ (η composed with the affine isometric embedding x ↦ Φ(s,x), then the continuous linear ℒ), and tsupport η^♭_s ⊆ {x : Φ(s,x) ∈ tsupport η}, which is compact (preimage of a compact set under a closed isometric embedding; compare SimonGMT `pointSlice_isTestForm`). So φ := (s ↦ η^♭_s) is admissible in Step 1 and Z(η) = ∫_0^1 X(η^♭_s) ds.
3. (Support of Z.) L₀ := Φ([0,1] × B̄_{R₀}(0)) is compact. If tsupport η ∩ L₀ = ∅, then for each s ∈ [0,1] the set N_s := {x : Φ(s,x) ∉ tsupport η} is open, contains B̄_{R₀}(0) ⊇ spt X, and η^♭_s = 0 on N_s; so tsupport η^♭_s ⊆ E ∖ N_s is disjoint from spt X and X(η^♭_s) = 0 by isoperimetric_apply_eq_zero_of_disjoint_support. By Step 2, Z(η) = 0. Consequently spt Z ⊆ L₀: for p ∉ L₀ choose r > 0 with B̄_r(p) ∩ L₀ = ∅ (L₀ is closed); W := B_r(p) is open, closure W = B̄_r(p) is compact, and Z vanishes on W, so p lies in the zero region of Z.
4. (The map h.) Let h : E′ → E, h(y) := y_0 · π(y), so h(Φ(s,x)) = s x. h is C^∞ (bilinear in the coordinates), i.e. ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) h. For compact K ⊆ E, h⁻¹(K) ∩ spt Z is closed (h continuous, K closed, spt Z closed in univ) and contained in the compact L₀, hence compact.
